text:
Jordan: quick heads-up — hit a regression + intermittent OOM on a 48GB A100 when we co-reside opt-1.3b + gpt-medium with KV-cache enabled after the recent kernel-selection patch.
Priya: ouch. regression in perf numbers or just OOMs?
Jordan: both. perf: throughput -18% overall for batching workload A, p99 latency +120ms. OOMs are when two long sequences arrive concurrently and kvcache prewarm kicks in.
Marco: which kernel change landed? the math-opt fallback or the new grouped-attn kernels?
Jordan: grouped-attn preference for seq<1024 was flipped to prefer kernel B over legacy. Kernel B reduces single-model latency but uses ~140MB more transient workspace on the matmul path.
Ava: that could push us over the soft partition thresholds. did allocator report fragmentation growth?
Jordan: yes — slab free list fragmentation jumped ~22% in the trace. Attached profiler snippet (trimmed):
```
[PROFILE] timeline: alloc_hot 0.0s -> 12.3s
kv_cache_reserve: 1.2GB
workspace_peak: 26.7GB
fragmented_free: 3.2GB
oom_before_evict: 1845557777:gpu0:oom
```
Priya: remind me — are we using workspace right-sizing per-model or a global target? I thought we had per-model workspace_reserve.
Jordan: we have per-model nominal workspace (computed from offline sim) but runtime uses dynamic growth with soft-reserve factor 1.0 -> now kernel B's temp usage spikes beyond reserve.
Tomas: can we fallback kernel selection when co-residency would violate reserve? i.e. if predicted peak > reserved -> choose smaller-kernel path.
Marco: that's feasible if we have a fast check: given seq_len and batch, estimate transient workspace and decision table. we already have percentile histograms for seq_len per route.
Ava: also KV-cache prewarm order matters: prewarm can allocate big contiguous buffers. Maybe evict non-hot KV shards first on pressure.
Priya: proposal: hybrid isolation policy — soft VRAM partitions by model with a small overcommit budget, plus a preemptive kvcache-evict slot that activates if free<1.5GB.
Jordan: rough numbers tested locally: with soft partitions + kernel fallback to legacy, throughput loss reduced to -5% and no OOM in 6k concurrent traces.
Marco: what's the cost of legacy kernel on long sequences? we might increase tail latency for those requests.
Jordan: yes p99 increases ~60ms on those long sequences but avoids OOM and overall throughput better.
Tomas: operationally: add a fast decision in runtime: estimate_workspace(seq_len,batch,model_variant) -> if estimate + current_alloc > partition_limit -> pick kernel_small or trigger kvcache-evict.
Priya: can we get the estimator from compile-time kernel metadata? we have per-kernel workspace_overhead numbers from kernel profiling job.
Ava: and add an async prefetch/evict strategy for kvcache: evict least-recently-used shards but keep a small hotset pinned. Use weighted eviction to prefer model B shards (less reused).
Jordan: I'll attach a minimal config snippet we used in the experiment:
```
allocator:
  soft_partition: true
  partition_map:
    opt-1.3b: 0.55
    gpt-medium: 0.35
  overcommit_budget: 0.10
kernel_fallback:
  enabled: true
  trigger_threshold_mb: 1536
kvcache:
  preemptive_evict_threshold_mb: 1536
  evict_policy: lru_weighted
```
Marco: nice. we should also add a metric for "kernel_workspace_headroom" so SRE can alert when headroom < 1GB repeatedly.
Ava: and a canary rollout: enable new kernel selection flags only for dedicated pools and run the co-residency perf suite.
Priya: action items: Jordan to open RFC with profiler traces + config; Marco to add estimator table glue to kernel selector; Tomas to implement kvcache weighted-evict; Ava to run e2e canary. I'll own the rollout plan.
Jordan: thanks — will post RFC and raw traces in this thread.
deploy-bot: incremental rollout started: kernel-selection:grouped-attn -> 10% hosts in us-west.
Priya: ping when RFC link is up, will sync with SRE on alerts.
Jordan: RFC: https://rwd.internal/rfcs/1845557777-vram-hybrid-isolation (uploading traces now)
Marco: copying the quick sim results to ticket. I'll prototype estimator in a branch.
Ava: planning canary run tomorrow 09:00 UTC against staging pool.
Tomas: if we need immediate mitigation, revert kernel ordering in the selector for co-resident pools.
Jordan: leaving that as a hotfix option. thanks all :thumbsup:
